relations: The hand grips the sphere cluster, maintaining a diverging V-shape that settles slightly before the upper chain bends downward.
The upper chain folds alongside the lower chain, initiating a parallel double-row merge that travels leftward across the frame.
As the merging front progresses, the open angle shrinks and the remaining diverging tails converge into a uniform strip.
The completed double-row strip remains largely unchanged, with the hand holding the cluster and highlights moving with the spheres.
caption: The video depicts a top-down view of a plain white surface where a right hand at the right edge grips a cluster of dark, glossy metallic spheres, from which two single-file chains extend leftward. At the start the chains diverge from the hand, creating an open V with an upper arm running near-horizontally toward the left edge and a lower arm angling down-left. For the first portion of the clip this two-arm configuration stays largely steady, with only slight settling of the chains. Then the upper arm begins to bend downward near the hand and folds alongside the lower arm, converting the single-file V into a parallel double-row strip. This merge starts at the hand side and the joining front travels leftward across the frame, gradually shrinking the open angle at the left. As the front reaches the far left, the two remaining diverging tails converge and join the double row, producing a uniform two-row strip spanning the width. After that the strip remains largely unchanged, with the hand at the right holding the cluster and little further rearrangement of the spheres. The specular highlights on the balls move with the spheres themselves.
